items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: That's the first time I ever met Meyer Davis

ctx.x: the famous band leaders on the marquees. You never got a chance to hear them, I guess, at that time.

No, no I didn't because, as I said, I, I go back, I went back to the re -- not the reser -- to Blue Island to, to visit my, my brother, and that one time my uncle ran into me, and he said to me it was gettin' on to school time in September. So he asked me what I wanted to go to school, or you want to go home. So I said I want to go home. So my uncle said, "All right, I'll buy you a ticket." And his advice to me was "go back to school when you get home." So that's how I came back to Arizona. And talk about trauma!…

playing, performing. And those years in Tucson was very instructive. I'm gettin' back to where I came from. I find myself temporarily where I came from, and in that way, I begin to be a little more aware of who I was, and my Indian-ness has never left me although I was away from the Indians in Chicago and I had forgotten my language.
